statement: Whenever number_of_alternating_groups(colors, k) returns a result r, with n = len(colors), r equals the number of integers s with 0 <= s < n such that for every integer j with 0 <= j <= k-2, colors[(s+j) mod n] != colors[(s+j+1) mod n]. Equivalently, r is the number of starting positions of k contiguous tiles in the circle whose colors alternate throughout the whole block.
preconditions: Let n = len(colors). n >= 3; for every i with 0 <= i < n, colors[i] is either 0 or 1; k is an integer with 3 <= k <= n. All cyclic indices are taken modulo n.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, number_of_alternating_groups(colors, k) returns a result r; it does not fail, panic, overflow, or access memory out of bounds.
preconditions: Let n = len(colors). n >= 3; for every i with 0 <= i < n, colors[i] is either 0 or 1; k is an integer with 3 <= k <= n. All cyclic indices are taken modulo n.

statement: Whenever number_of_alternating_groups(colors, k) returns r, then 0 <= r <= len(colors).
preconditions: Let n = len(colors). n >= 3; for every i with 0 <= i < n, colors[i] is either 0 or 1; k is an integer with 3 <= k <= n. All cyclic indices are taken modulo n.

statement: Whenever number_of_alternating_groups(colors, k) returns r, r = len(colors) if and only if for every i with 0 <= i < len(colors), colors[i] != colors[(i+1) mod len(colors)].
preconditions: Let n = len(colors). n >= 3; for every i with 0 <= i < n, colors[i] is either 0 or 1; k is an integer with 3 <= k <= n. All cyclic indices are taken modulo n.

statement: If colors[i] = colors[0] for every i with 0 <= i < len(colors), then whenever number_of_alternating_groups(colors, k) returns r, r = 0.
preconditions: Let n = len(colors). n >= 3; for every i with 0 <= i < n, colors[i] is either 0 or 1; k is an integer with 3 <= k <= n. All cyclic indices are taken modulo n.

statement: Whenever number_of_alternating_groups(colors, k) returns r, r = 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(colors). n >= 3; for every i with 0 <= i < n, colors[i] is either 0 or 1; k = len(colors); and there is exactly one integer i with 0 <= i < len(colors) and colors[i] = colors[(i+1) mod len(colors)]. All cyclic indices are taken modulo n.

statement: Whenever number_of_alternating_groups(colors, k) returns r, r = 0.

statement: Whenever number_of_alternating_groups(colors, k) returns r, 0 <= r <= 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(colors). n >= 3; for every i with 0 <= i < n, colors[i] is either 0 or 1; len(colors) is odd; k = len(colors). All cyclic indices are taken modulo n.

statement: Let t be any integer and define an array colors' of the same length by colors'[i] = colors[(i+t) mod n] for 0 <= i < n. If number_of_alternating_groups(colors, k) returns r and number_of_alternating_groups(colors', k) returns r', then r = r'.
